factors.name: Choice-dominated vs. mixed/parallel branching
factors.summary: All four retained measures load strongly on this single factor (|loading| 0.72–1.00), so it is the general factor of this reduced set, but with mixed signs. Connector Heterogeneity (-0.995), Density (-0.886) and Token split (-0.773) decrease as the factor increases, while Control flow complexity (+0.723) increases. Higher scores therefore mark sparser nets with many choice-split arcs, little parallel token splitting and homogeneous connector types, and lower scores mark denser nets that mix parallel and choice connectors. Because Size was removed, the density side cannot be checked against net size.

interpretation.overall: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO of 0.72 is above the 0.6 threshold, so the data are suitable for a factor analysis. One factor was extracted, matching the suggestion: only the first eigenvalue (3.14) exceeds 1, and the second is 0.59. The factor explains 72% of the variance of the four retained measures, with no cross-loadings or unassigned measures. Connector Heterogeneity is almost fully explained (communality 0.99). Control flow complexity (0.52) and Token split (0.60) keep substantial unique variance. The factor contrasts choice-heavy, sparse nets with dense nets that mix parallel and choice connectors.
caveats: Eight of the twelve non-constant measures, including Size, Sequentiality and Separability, were removed by the MSA filter, so the factor describes only a narrow slice of model complexity.
With only four measures, a single factor is nearly unavoidable and says little about the dimensional structure of model complexity as a whole.
Bartlett's df of 66 corresponds to twelve measures, so the test appears to have been computed before the MSA filtering and may not describe the final four-measure set.
The loadings have mixed signs, so the factor is a contrast between kinds of nets rather than a single 'more complex' direction.
Connector Heterogeneity is undefined for nets without connectors, and the result depends on how such nets were handled.
The result reflects shared variance in these 288 discovered nets and depends on the discovery algorithms that produced them; it does not show causal relations.
